title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBR
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates the standard process for enterprise customer onboarding, the escalation path for production incidents, integration checklist and common known issues, and the templates used for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and on-call SRE engineers who participate in enterprise onboarding and operational support.

Scope: Applies to all customers who sign a Dedicated or Private contract, and to large hosted customers on enterprise SLAs.

Summary of key outcomes:
- A reproducible onboarding timeline (0–90 days) with ownership for each milestone.
- An escalation playbook with clear contact matrix and response targets.
- A pre-integration checklist and sample config snippets for common integration patterns (API, Dedicated, Private).
- A curated list of known issues and recommended workarounds for frequently seen customer problems.
- Health check cadence and QBR templates to drive customer success metrics and renewal conversations.

1) Onboarding phases and timeline (0–90 days)

Phase 0: Agreement & kickoff (Day 0–7)
- Owners: AE (sales), CS Manager, SE.
- Deliverables: signed SOW, initial kickoff meeting scheduled, security questionnaire received.
- Action items:
  - Schedule 60–90 minute kickoff with agenda (Intro, goals, success criteria, timeline, points of contact).
  - Provision initial test accounts / API keys and enable logging to customer telemetry (if agreed).
  - Send security & network requirements doc.

Phase 1: Discovery & environment setup (Day 7–21)
- Owners: SE, CS.
- Deliverables: integration plan, network firewall/IP allowlist, KMS/HSM key exchange (if Private).
- Action items:
  - Run tech discovery: expected QPS, average request size, P95 latency targets, privacy/regulatory constraints.
  - For Dedicated/Private: confirm VPC peering, egress rules, and machine image access.
  - For hosted: confirm API access pattern, keys, and rate limit expectations.

Phase 2: Integration & validation (Day 21–60)
- Owners: SE, CS, Customer Engineers.
- Deliverables: integration checklist completed, end-to-end validation runs, initial production pilot.
- Action items:
  - Execute integration checklist (see section 4).
  - Run 2–4 pilot scenarios with representative production prompts. Capture latency, token usage, error rate.
  - Flag any model quality regressions to Applied ML and add to evaluation sets.

Phase 3: Ramp & SLA handoff (Day 60–90)
- Owners: CS, SRE, Account Team.
- Deliverables: SLA confirmation, on-call paging configured, runbook shared.
- Action items:
  - Confirm production telemetry in Redwood Console dashboards (latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens).
  - Schedule formal handoff: support routing, escalation contacts, and QBR cadence.
  - Ensure playbooks and runbooks are accessible in customer-specific Confluence space when required.

2) Roles & responsibilities (quick reference)
- Customer Success (owner): onboarding project manager, owner of success metrics, QBR facilitator.
- Solutions Engineering: lead technical integrator, API guidance, test plan owner.
- Support (owner): fix triage, ticket lifecycle owner for P1/P2.
- SRE/Platform: on-call for production incidents, capacity planning for Dedicated pools.
- Applied ML/Research: model quality regressions and evaluation triage.

3) Escalation playbook (production incident flow)

Severity definitions and targets:
- P0 / Sev1 (Platform outage / customer-facing application down): initial response <= 15 min, P1 page to on-call SRE + CS alert, full cross-functional war room within 60 min.
- P1 / Sev2 (Degraded performance causing significant user impact): initial response <= 30 min, CS informed, remediation target 4 hours with continuous updates.
- P2 / Sev3 (Partial degradation, non-critical errors): acknowledge <= 4 hours, fix or mitigation within 3 business days.

Escalation contact matrix (primary -> secondary):
- Customer Success (CS): cs-owners@redwood.example -> cs-ops@redwood.example
- Support triage queue: support-enterprise@redwood.example -> support-oncall@redwood.example
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall-pager (PagerDuty) -> sre-rotation-backup (PagerDuty)
- SE escalation (technical): se-leads@redwood.example -> solutions-esc@redwood.example

Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Triage and classify severity using the incident classifier checklist below.
2. If Sev1/Sev2: open an incident channel (Slack #inc-customer-<short-name>), invite SRE, CS, SE, and Support.
3. Post initial status update in channel within 15 minutes (incident summary, impact, mitigation in progress, next update ETA).
4. For Sev1: start live troubleshooting, capture core dumps/profiles, initiate fallback policies (route to model-variant or region).
5. For all severities: create support ticket in Zendesk/Service system, log incident ID in channel and update customer-facing status page if required.
6. After mitigation, run post-incident RCA within 72 hours for Sev1 and Sev2.

Incident classifier checklist (quick):
- Is traffic failing for all customers or a single customer?
- Are errors > 1% of requests or latency P95 > 3x baseline?
- Is there data loss or model corruption?
- Is a security breach suspected?

4) Integration checklist (pre-flight & validation)

Pre-flight (network & security):
- Confirm allowlisted IPs/CIDR for Dedicated/Private endpoints.
- Confirm TLS termination and cert pinning requirements.
- Exchange KMS/HSM configuration if using customer-managed keys.
- Ensure logging and audit-logging endpoints configured for compliance.

API & perf validation:
- Confirm API keys, rate limits, and account quotas.
- Run representative throughput test: 10–20% of expected steady-state QPS for 30 minutes to validate autoscaling behavior.
- Validate token accounting and cost metrics in Redwood Console.
- Validate streaming responses and function calling behavior if used.

Model & quality checks:
- Run evaluation set with representative prompts; capture accuracy/quality metrics and compare vs baseline.
- Confirm fallback model variants for degraded capacity (e.g., gptx-16q -> gptx-8q).

Example CLI snippet (curl) to validate endpoint:
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"Hello world"}'

5) Known issues & recommended workarounds (selection of frequent cases)

Issue: Streaming responses unexpectedly truncated
- Symptoms: client receives EOF before final token, no error code returned.
- Root cause (common): reverse proxy or load balancer timeout on long-lived connections.
- Workaround: increase idle/streaming timeout on LB (recommended 120s), and enable resumable stream fallback in client.
- Owner: eng-platform / SRE.

Issue: Token accounting mismatch between customer instrumentation and Redwood Console
- Symptoms: customer reports higher token consumption than console shows.
- Root cause (common): local pre/post processing (prompt template expansion) not accounted for on server.
- Workaround: instrument client to log pre-send token counts and reconcile after 24–48 hours. Provide sample tokenization snippet in appendix.
- Owner: SE / Support.

Issue: Dedicated pool cold-start latency spikes after low-traffic period
- Symptoms: P95 latency spikes to 3–6x baseline for first 30–60 seconds after idle.
- Root cause: GPU warmup and model weight activation.
- Workaround: configure warmup pings (cron job at low QPS) or enable reserved minimum instances for Dedicated pools.
- Owner: eng-infra / Dedicated ops.

Issue: Private deployment upgrade fails due to image signature mismatch
- Symptoms: upgrade aborts with signature verification error.
- Workaround: confirm image tag integrity and re-run unpack step; if using offline air-gapped installation, re-transfer signed artifact via secure channel.
- Owner: eng-private-deployments.

6) Support process & ticket lifecycle

Ticket routing:
- All enterprise incoming issues should create a ticket in Zendesk with tag "enterprise" and customer account ID.
- Support Triage team annotates ticket with initial severity and assigns to SE or SRE if technical.

SLA commitments (customer-facing):
- P0 / Sev1: initial response 15 min, updates every 30 min until mitigated.
- P1 / Sev2: initial response 30 min, updates every 2 hours during remediation window.
- P2 / Sev3: initial response within 4 hours during business hours.

Escalation timeline inside Redwood (internal):
- If no progress within 2 hours for a P1: escalate to SRE on-call and CS director.
- If no resolution for P2 after 72 hours: open internal incident review and add to weekly triage.

Post-incident actions:
- For Sev1/Sev2: owner schedules RCA and mitigation plan within 72 hours. Add follow-up actions to the backlog and assign an owner.
- For Sev3: document incident and include in monthly support retrospective.

7) Health checks & QBR materials (templates and cadence)

Health check cadence:
- Weekly lightweight health snapshot for active pilots (1 pager): traffic, token usage, error rate, latency, cost delta. Owner: CS.
- Monthly health review for live production customers: deeper dashboard review (billing trends, cost per 1k tokens, model quality regressions). Owner: CS + SE.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR): executive summary, roadmap alignment, SLA adherence, renewal health score. Owner: CS manager.

Health check 1-pager template (fields):
- Date range
- Executive summary (1–2 sentences)
- Key metrics: Avg QPS, 95th latency (ms), error rate (%), cost / 1k tokens, usage growth (%)
- Recent incidents (last 90d) and status
- Open action items (owner + ETA)
- Recommendations and next steps

QBR agenda (60 minutes recommended):
1. Welcome and executive summary (5 min)
2. Business review: usage, ROI, and metrics vs goals (10 min)
3. Technical review: performance, incidents, and model quality (15 min)
4. Roadmap & upcoming product changes that impact customer (10 min)
5. Risks and mitigation (5 min)
6. Success plan and milestones for next quarter (10 min)
7. Action items and owners (5 min)

Renewal health scoring (example factors):
- Adoption: 40% (API traffic growth, production usage)
- Reliability: 25% (incidents & SLA compliance)
- Cost predictability: 15% (variance vs forecast)
- Strategic alignment: 20% (product roadmap fit)

8) Communication templates (examples)

Initial kickoff invite (subject): Redwood Onboarding Kickoff — <Customer Name>
Body snippet: "Thanks for the partnership — please find the kickoff agenda attached. Goal: confirm success criteria, timeline, and participants. Action: please complete the security questionnaire before the meeting."

P1 incident status update (subject): P1 Incident — <Customer Name> — 30 minute update
Body snippet: "Current impact: X% of requests returning 5xx. Mitigation in progress: scaling fallback and backlog drain. Next update: in 30 minutes. Incident ID: R-ID-XXXXX."

9) Appendix: useful dashboards, links and sample commands

Dashboards to verify after onboarding:
- Console -> Customer -> Usage & Billing (token trends and cost)
- Console -> Models -> Latency by endpoint (P50/P95/P99)
- Console -> Alerts -> Active alerts and recent incidents

Sample tokenization snippet (Python) for reconciliation:
from redwood_tokenizer import tokenize
prompt = f"system: ...\nuser: Hello world"
print(len(tokenize(prompt)))

Contact list (internal):
- CS escalation alias: cs-ops@redwood.example
- Support triage: support-enterprise@redwood.example
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.example (PagerDuty)
- Security incident response: security-incident@redwood.example

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Maya Thompson (CS) — update this document after each major onboarding or after any Sev1/Sev2 RCA.
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any enterprise SLA change.

Notes and references:
- See also: enterprise-onboarding-support-playbook-2026 for historical runbooks, and enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026 for detailed integration templates.

End of playbook.
